verification.check: Risk Brain's service account holds secretAccessor only on its own secrets, and no Risk Brain credential appears in any Reflex package manifest.

notes: This entry comes from H's regional-cell edges. Secret Manager/KMS has one security edge to the Reflex Package Agent, for signing and verification, and a separate one to Risk Brain. The requirement is read from the diagram alone; neither PDF states it. Conflicts C3 and C7 apply, because Risk Brain is not a separate service in the tree (ADR 0091). Priority P1: master Phase 3 (Risk Brain) and GCP Phase 6.

title: Organization Policy restricts which Google APIs may be enabled
statement: Organization Policy restricts the Google Cloud APIs that may be enabled to an approved list.
rationale: Every enabled API adds attack surface and is another place data can go. An allow-list stops a project from quietly enabling a service nobody reviewed.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, node 'org' ('Restrict APIs')

verification.check: The plan sets a constraint at organization or folder level (gcp.restrictServiceUsage or an equivalent custom constraint) that limits enabled services to the approved list.

notes: This entry is split from H's Organization Policies node, which names four constraint categories. The other three are SEC-067 to SEC-069. In the tree modules/services enables APIs per environment from a map that gives a reason for each API. That is review, not a guardrail. Priority P0: GCP Phase 0.

title: Organization Policy restricts resources to approved regions
statement: Organization Policy restricts resource creation to the platform's approved regions.
rationale: A resource in an unapproved region can put data outside its legal residency and outside the network design. A location constraint refuses such a resource when someone tries to create it.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, node 'org' ('regions')

verification.check: The plan sets gcp.resourceLocations at organization or folder level to the approved regions, and an attempt to create a resource elsewhere in a test project is refused.

notes: This entry is split from H's Organization Policies node. Residency is also a v2.1 ledger concern: G p10 chooses the ledger's leader region by legal residency. The tree pins each module to var.region and has no organization. Priority P0: GCP Phase 0.

title: Organization Policy restricts external IP addresses
statement: Organization Policy restricts which VM instances may have external IP addresses and denies them by default.
rationale: An external address on a VM is a direct path around the load balancer, Cloud Armor and IAP. Denying external addresses by policy means their absence is enforced, not just remembered.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, node 'org' ('external IPs')

verification.check: The plan sets compute.vmExternalIpAccess at organization or folder level to deny all, or to an explicit list of instances.

notes: This entry is split from H's Organization Policies node. In the tree the execution node deliberately has no access_config and therefore no external address. That is the property this constraint would enforce. Priority P0: GCP Phase 0.

title: Organization Policy constrains service-account and workload-identity behaviour
statement: Organization Policy constrains how service accounts behave, and it constrains the IAM and Workload Identity configuration that governs them.
rationale: While policy still permits key creation, 'no service-account keys' is a habit rather than a guarantee. Constraining it at the organization makes the keyless posture of SEC-034 and SEC-035 structural.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, node 'org' ('service account behavior')
VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, edge org→iam

verification.check: The plan sets iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation, iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload, iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts and iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders at organization or folder level.

notes: This entry merges the service-account clause of H's Organization Policies node with H's Organization Policies→IAM + Workload Identity edge. It turns SEC-035 from an absence into an impossibility. The tree has no organization. Priority P0: GCP Phase 0.

title: Reflex and Fabric VMs run as Shielded VMs
statement: Reflex and Fabric compute runs on Shielded VMs with secure boot, vTPM and integrity monitoring enabled.
rationale: A modified boot chain or kernel on a node that holds venue sessions or broker journals would be invisible to everything running above it. Measured boot and integrity monitoring make that kind of tampering detectable.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, node 'shield'
VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, edge policy→shield

verification.check: Every Reflex and Fabric instance template in the plan enables secure boot, vTPM and integrity monitoring.

notes: This entry merges the Shielded half of H's Shielded/Confidential VM node with H's Admission/NetworkPolicy→Shielded VM edge, which extends the runtime-control boundary from GKE to VM compute. GCP-059 holds the same requirement with G p17's catalogue row. KUBERNETES and MANAGED_SERVICE, carried in with the edge, were dropped because this is a VM setting. In the tree modules/execution-node sets enable_secure_boot, enable_vtpm and enable_integrity_monitoring. No Fabric VM exists. Priority P0: GCP Phases 2 and 3.

title: Reflex and Fabric VMs use Confidential VM where compatible
statement: Reflex and Fabric compute runs as Confidential VM wherever the chosen machine type supports it.
rationale: Confidential VM encrypts memory against the host, which protects venue session keys and journal contents from a compromised hypervisor. The requirement is conditional because not every machine type supports it.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, node 'shield' ('where compatible')

verification.check: For each Reflex and Fabric machine type, the register records whether Confidential VM is supported. Where it is, a benchmark shows its effect on decision p99 before it is enabled.

notes: This entry is split from H's Shielded/Confidential VM node. GCP-059 chose not to make Confidential VM an obligation, and it is kept here only as a conditional one. Priority P3, as an optional hardening: no phase exit names it, and it must first be shown not to break the Reflex latency budget.

title: Google API access from inside the perimeter uses Private Service Connect or the restricted VIP
statement: The Private Service Connect endpoints through which workloads reach Google APIs sit inside the VPC Service Controls perimeter and resolve to the restricted API surface.
rationale: A perimeter is only as strong as the path workloads use to reach the APIs it protects. If private access resolved to the unrestricted endpoints, services the perimeter is meant to protect would be reachable without its checks.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, edge vpcsc→psc

verification.check: *.googleapis.com resolves, through the private DNS zone, to a Private Service Connect endpoint targeting the vpc-sc bundle or to restricted.googleapis.com at 199.36.153.4/30. The firewall and route rules that admit Google API traffic name that same range.

notes: This entry comes from H's VPC Service Controls→Private Service Connect edge. SEC-047 holds the perimeter itself. DEFECT FOUND IN THE TREE while writing this entry. Google's Private Google Access documentation (docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/configure-private-google-access, read 2026-09-25) gives restricted.googleapis.com as 199.36.153.4/30 and private.googleapis.com as 199.36.153.8/30. modules/network publishes the A record restricted.googleapis.com as 199.36.153.8 to 199.36.153.11, which is the private range, and points *.googleapis.com at it with a CNAME. modules/trust-zones, modules/execution-node, modules/connectivity and modules/gitops-control-plane all treat 199.36.153.8/30 as 'the restricted VIP'. Workloads that resolve Google APIs through that zone therefore reach the private VIP. The private VIP also serves APIs that no perimeter can protect, which is the reverse of what the module comments intend. The finding is not fixed here, because this task writes requirements. Priority P1, with SEC-047.

title: A workload receives runtime secrets only after admission and network policy admit it
statement: Runtime access to Secret Manager is tied to admission and network policy. A workload obtains its secrets only if admission policy has admitted it and network policy permits its path to Secret Manager.
rationale: If an unadmitted workload, such as an unsigned image started by hand, could still mount production secrets, admission control would stop the image and then hand it the credentials anyway.

sources.section: VIEWS.security — 06 · Network, Security & Trust Boundaries, edge secret→policy

verification.check: In a test cluster, a pod from an unattested image, or from outside the governed namespaces, is refused at admission and never receives the secret. The admitted workload with the same service account mounts it.

notes: This entry comes from H's Secret Manager→Admission/NetworkPolicy edge. The reading is this entry's own, since neither PDF states the coupling. The admission half is SEC-037, and G p12 §13's sandboxing (NetworkPolicy and egress policy) is related. Conflict C3 applies. On Cloud Run the tree gets the equivalent by construction: the Binary Authorization policy refuses an unattested revision, so there is no revision to mount a secret. Priority P1: the requirement applies once warm GKE services consume secrets (GCP Phase 6).
